description: Update README.md to document the rule-based prediction engine and create app_rule.py terminal application that uses the rule engine for predictions.
steps: Step 1: Update README.md to add a section documenting the rule-based prediction engine, its usage, and how it relates to the ML pipeline
Step 2: Create app_rule.py - a terminal application following the same pattern as app.py but using the rule engine for predictions, supporting single and batch predictions from the command line
Step 3: Verify both files work correctly - parse without errors, rule engine predictions succeed
acceptance_criteria: README.md documents the rule-based prediction engine module
app_rule.py exists and uses rule_engine for predictions
app_rule.py supports single and batch predictions
app_rule.py follows the same style/pattern as app.py
All Python files parse without syntax errors
Rule engine predictions work from app_rule.py
verification: Run: python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('app_rule.py').read())" to verify syntax
Run: python app_rule.py --help or similar to verify it loads
Run: python -c "from rule_engine.engine import RuleEngine; e = RuleEngine(); print(e.predict({'Cr': 17.5, 'Ni': 8.5}))" to verify engine works
findings: Both app_rule.py and README.md created/updated successfully. All 158 existing tests continue to pass. The app_rule.py supports --predict, --batch, --list-rules, --rules-for, --info, --threshold flags plus interactive mode. README now documents the rule engine with usage examples, API code snippets, and a comparison table between ML and rule-based approaches.
